submit.headline: Flood limits first - 600 mm shell needed for envelope
submit.summary: K 2750 (ProcessColumn-1: 500 mm ID, 14 000 mm, 6 bar / 150 °C) is tight at +20 % feed and fails the +10 % operating envelope. With bottoms held at 3.0 mol/s flood is 0.79 vs 0.80 = 98.8 % at 1.2× and 1.008 vs 0.80 = 126 % at 1.32× (K2750_1p2_scaled_500, K2750_1p32_fixed_500) and base split is lost. Ratio-controlled bottoms 3.0→3.6 mol/s at 1.2× (3.96 at 1.32×) holds purity and 600 mm ID gives 0.604 vs 0.80 = 75.5 % at 1.32× (K2750_1p32_600_verify) with +20 % duty (+32 % at envelope) and all documented P/T checks < 61 %.

proposals.title: Hold base split - ratio-control bottoms withdrawal
proposals.why: Fixed 3.0 mol/s loses base split (45.1→50+ mol% Water in bottoms) at +20 % feed. Scaling to 3.6 mol/s at 1.2× (3.96 at 1.32× envelope, i.e. 3.0 * FEED/1000 kg/h) holds base split with reflux 1.5. Verified at 1.2× 0.79 vs 0.80 =98.8 % (K2750_1p2_scaled_500) and at 1.32× 0.643-0.604 vs 0.80 with 600 mm shell (K2750_1p32_600_verify). Implement as feed-forward ratio control FEED flow → bottoms SP. No capex.

proposals.title: Replace column with 600 mm ID rated shell (vendor to confirm)

changes.basis: DWSIM Fair flood requires 0.638 m at 1.32× scaled 3.96 mol/s; 600 mm uniform (next standard matching KX 2750 600 mm section) gives 0.604 vs 0.80 =75.5 % at envelope (K2750_1p32_600_verify) and 0.549 =68.6 % at 1.2× (K2750_1p2_600 family); 525 mm gives 0.789 =98.6 % no margin (K2750_1p32_525). Height 14000 mm, 6 bar/150 °C, 1.4571, 15 stages same.

proposals.why: Existing 500 mm ID cannot pass the +10 % operating envelope even with correct split: 0.869 vs 0.80 =108.6 % at 1.32× scaled (K2750_1p32_scaled_500) and 1.008 =126 % fixed (K2750_1p32_fixed_500). All documented P/T checks pass (<61 % at 1.32×) so flooding and purity are the only documented limits. New 600 mm ID provides required capacity with margin; vendor to confirm tray/valve design, downcomers, nozzles for line 2750.001.6 and *at N3*/*C2* valve.

submit.why: 500 mm column cannot pass envelope (flood >100 % and purity drift) - a larger shell is required; operating change alone only suffices for nominal 1.2×. 600 mm shell passes all documented checks at 1.32× with ~25 % flood margin.
